content:
ana: Pushed the fast-revoke probe results. TL;DR: revoke fastpath reduces leakage but borrow-pool allocator still handed out ~3 grants in worst case.
jordan: Paste the traces / minimal logs?
ana: (actually ana) trace=probe-4f7, logs attached in gist: https://gists.example/probe-4f7 - main failure window ~80-120ms.
mike: Interesting. So not 12s like before, but still >0. What was the sequence?
ana: Sequence: 1) admission marks tenant PROBATION and emits revoke_v1 (decision_id=did-987) 2) revoke consumed by token-service fast consumer (latency ~8ms) 3) borrow-pool allocator had 3 inflight borrow requests already in local queue and granted them before pool-stop flag applied.
kelsey: That explains it. Fast consumer stops issuing new grants but it doesn't atomically clear local allocator queues. We need an in-process interrupt for allocator drains.
jordan: Two mitigation ideas: (A) atomic pool-stop + drain handshake where allocator checks a stop bit before every grant; (B) preemptive revoke that injects negative credits into pool balance to make grants fail. Tradeoffs?
mike: A is cleaner but requires allocator hot-path check (tiny cost). B is clever but can cause transient negative accounting headaches.
kelsey: I prototyped A: add `pool_state: STOPPED` in revoke payload and allocator consults memory-mapped flag. Measured overhead ~0.7% on qps.
ana: Probe measured leakage window median 45ms, p99 140ms. After A prototype, leakage median 6ms, p99 22ms.
jordan: Good. Does A require cross-service coordination for durable stop? What about restarts?
kelsey: We persist last_decision_id in pool-meta store. On restart allocator loads last_decision and enforces STOPPED until decision TTL expires.
mike: Also add epoch on tokens: token_epoch=N in token metadata. Admission increments epoch on revoke. Edge: clock skew if relying on timestamps.
jordan: Agree use monotonic epoch per tenant. Token issuance includes epoch. Runtime can compare and reject older epoch tokens.
ana: Metrics to add: pool-stop-ops, grants-after-pool-stop, pool-drain-time, token-epoch-mismatch. Alert if grants-after-pool-stop > 0.
kelsey: Small UX: clients hitting in-flight grants should see `429` with `Retry-After` and `x-reason: probation` header.
mike: We also need retention of revoke events long enough to handle slow consumers. Suggest keep revoke_v1 for 2 mins in topic.
jordan: Operational checklist: - land allocator stop-bit check - update revoke_v1 payload with `pool_state` + `decision_id` + `epoch` - persist last_decision in pool-meta - add token_epoch to tokens - add metrics/alerts - run 12h synthetic with varying borrow pool sizes
infra-bot: canary deploy scheduled: token-service allocator-drain patch to staging at 2026-03-25T01:15Z
ana: I'll run the synthetic tonight and report p50/p99. Thanks all.
